meta.title: Telemetry-first independent release decision
meta.scope: Review v0.1, defer a paper, build consented real-project telemetry, and publish a privacy-safe independent pilot.
exclusions: No causal model or effort comparison before real observations exist
No prompts, responses, code, diffs, logs, paths, file names, credentials, or personal data
No mutation of the predecessor pull request

decision_problem.project_classification: reversible public developer-tool pilot with local privacy-sensitive metadata
decision_problem.risk_level: high because public release and longitudinal observation can create privacy and evidence-quality harm
decision_problem.decision_owner: the user and GitHub repository owner AIALRA-0
decision_problem.desired_outcome: Collect enough consented real-project metadata for a later whole-machine analysis without premature model claims.
decision_problem.current_state: v0.1 has a deterministic router and manual analyzer but no automatic consented start-finish lifecycle or de-identified machine snapshot.
decision_problem.decision: Whether to publish an independent telemetry-first Skill now and postpone research conclusions until review gates are reached.
success_metrics: Collection stays disabled until explicit local enablement
A full synthetic lifecycle exposes no workspace identity in records or snapshots
The public repository has bilingual entrypoints, security policy, license, CI, tests, schemas, and evidence limits
A later status report distinguishes runs, projects, active days, routes, malformed records, and unknown usage
No model win-rate or causal claim appears before the review gate
constraints: Fixed categories and non-negative measurements only
Raw records remain local and the runtime has no uploader
Standalone GitHub repository with redaction checks
No research paper in this phase
irreversible_actions: Public Git history can persist after repository deletion

research_budget.overall_limit: One 2026-08-25 release audit bounded to official guidance, primary research, telemetry standards, GitHub prior art, and the supplied artifact.
paid_or_private_access: Authenticated access to the user's GitHub repositories
No paid patent or market database
research_budget.cutoff_policy: Stop novelty expansion after direct near matches disprove router uniqueness; preserve causal questions for the later dataset.

reversal_evidence: A record or snapshot contains prohibited content or a stable public identifier
A close predecessor already provides the same consented privacy-minimized lifecycle
Users cannot understand or control enable, disable, snapshot, and purge

questions.internal_probe: Inspect consent, schema, pseudonyms, snapshot suppression, deletion, and tests.

claims.statement: v0.1 lacks the requested consented automatic telemetry lifecycle.
claims.falsifier: The hashed artifact contains enable, start, finish, status, snapshot, and purge.

claims.statement: Sol, Terra, and Luna task routing is public prior art.
claims.falsifier: The cited repositories postdate this release or do not route the same model family.

claims.statement: Available evidence does not justify universal xhigh because agentic overthinking can reduce performance and local evaluation is required.
claims.falsifier: Representative local evaluation shows xhigh dominates on quality, rework, scope, latency, and usage.

claims.statement: v0.2 enforces disabled-by-default and content exclusion in tested paths.
claims.falsifier: A test finds prohibited text, a path, an unsafe run identifier, or a stable snapshot identifier.

claims.statement: The 50-run gate is an operational trigger, not guaranteed statistical power or causality.
claims.falsifier: A preregistered power analysis establishes sufficiency for a defined endpoint and effect size.

assumptions.statement: The Skill will run across enough representative projects.
assumptions.decision_impact: Otherwise summaries describe a selected minority.
assumptions.falsifier: After 14 active days many eligible tasks lack records or active runs are abandoned.

assumptions.statement: Fixed categories capture enough confounding structure for an initial descriptive review.
The host exposes usage measurements often enough.
assumptions.decision_impact: Without them only quality and rework can be analyzed.
assumptions.falsifier: Most runs remain unavailable or use incomparable definitions.

assumptions.statement: Pseudonym removal and small-group suppression sufficiently reduce disclosure risk.
assumptions.decision_impact: Otherwise snapshots stay private or categories are coarsened.
assumptions.falsifier: A review re-identifies a project from rare combinations.

recommendation.action: Publish and install v0.2.0 as a telemetry-first pilot, enable local-only collection, and start real data on the next complete iteration; defer the paper and comparisons.
recommendation.rationale: The router is useful but v0.1 overstates its observation loop; close prior art makes routing non-unique; a consented content-free lifecycle is the minimum next step.
recommendation.strongest_counterevidence: Skill-triggered observations are selected by task and user behavior, so route outcome rates remain confounded after count gates.
recommendation.minimum_test: Pass a synthetic lifecycle and one next-project real lifecycle, then inspect records and snapshots for prohibited content and identifiers.
recommendation.failure_response: Disable collection, retain or purge by user choice, fix the lifecycle, and restart without publishing comparisons.
recommendation.reversal_condition: Pause if sensitive content appears, runs cannot close, deletion control fails, or independent review finds material re-identification risk.

review_triggers: 2 actual routes with at least 10 runs each
Any prohibited content or stable snapshot identifier
More than 10 percent of completed work lacks a finish record
A host update changes model names, effort levels, or usage definitions
Independent privacy review produces repository-specific findings
